evaluations.label: A
errors: "Mark Knopf: project manager" - surname Knopf never said; only "Mark"
"Dirk Mengveld" - transcript says Dirk Meinfeld
"Xavier Jökens" - transcript says Xavier Juergens
"UI designer also present (name not captured)" - he introduced himself as Nick Broer
"Dolphin: freedom, openness" - 'openness' not stated; he said freedom, ocean, swimming
"rational changes only" - garbled transcript; the point was to avoid revolutionary changes, not that rational changes are the rule
strengths: Clear, well-organized sections covering goals, price, roles, process and early design considerations
Correctly records scope as TV-only, accessibility, lightweight material, and both price figures
Mentions next meeting in 30 minutes and assignments coming from the personal coach
weaknesses: Several misspelled or invented surnames and the UI designer's name missed
No explicit action items with owners; Dirk's pending marketing ideas not captured

evaluations.label: B
errors: "kick off TS3012a" - project code never mentioned in the transcript
PM called "Markoff"; he only said "Mark"
"Savier" / "Savier Jokins" and "Dirk Mangfelt" - names wrong (Xavier Juergens, Dirk Meinfeld)
UI designer referred to as "Speaker 4" though he gave his name, Nick Broer
Open question "Should the device be designed as a multi-remote control or limited strictly to television functions?" - this was settled: TV only
"Speaker 4 clarifies that the scope of the project is limited to a TV remote control" - the UI designer asked; the PM clarified
"Savier Jokins suggests using lightweight materials that are aesthetically impactful" - 'aesthetically impactful' not said
"Markoff introduced the team" - each member introduced themselves
strengths: Detailed outline covering kickoff, process, whiteboard training, icebreaker, constraints and next steps
Captures both price figures, three-phase process, project folder for minutes
Mentions accessibility, intuitive design and lightweight material
weaknesses: Contradicts itself: lists TV-only scope as open while also saying it was clarified
Action items have no owners and are generic restatements of the brief
Many name errors and 'Speaker 4' placeholder reduce usefulness; repetitive between summary and outline
Omits that the personal coach hands out assignments and that Dirk owes marketing ideas

evaluations.label: C
errors: "Dirk Mengveld" in action items - surname is Meinfeld
"The interface designer urged familiarity and rational changes" - transcript garbled; intent was no revolutionary changes
"Dirk chose an elephant as a market image" - he chose it for being big and strong; the PM made the market link (later line states this correctly)
"They set a €25 selling price" - the PM presented the given targets rather than the team setting them
strengths: Most faithful to the transcript, with correct attributions (PM confirmed TV-only scope, Mark agreed accessibility should be considered)
Captures the UI designer's comment that the budget leaves little room, Dirk's unprepared marketing ideas, and the personal coach giving assignments
Timestamps and summary-first structure make it easy to scan and verify
Action item for Dirk is grounded in what he said
weaknesses: UI designer's name (Nick Broer) not given
Some timestamps are coarse (several items tagged [01:08])
Only one action item; PM's commitment to post minutes not listed as an action

evaluations.label: D
errors: "Mark Knopp" - surname never said
"Xavier Juukens" and "Dirk Mankveld" - names wrong (Juergens, Meinfeld)
"Dolphin: freedom, smooth design" - 'smooth design' not said about the dolphin
Action item "Mark Knopp - Provide personal assignments to team members" - the personal coach gives assignments, not Mark
Action items "Xavier - Address material considerations" and "UI Designer - Prepare intuitive design concepts" are not assignments made in the meeting
Timestamps misplaced, e.g. scope clarified at (10:34) when it was at 11:32; Mark's action at (13:53) after the meeting ended
strengths: Compact and scannable; covers scope, intuitive design, accessibility, light material, pricing and the 30-minute break
Correctly notes the whiteboard was low-responsive and the PM will share minutes in the project files
weaknesses: Action items list is largely invented and misattributes who hands out assignments
Terse fragments give little context to someone who missed the meeting

rationale: C is the most accurate and best attributed, captures the key numbers, scope decision, accessibility and material points, the personal coach and Dirk's pending marketing ideas, with only minor issues. A is clean and broadly correct but invents or misspells surnames, misses the UI designer's name and gives no owned action items. B is thorough but adds an unsupported project code, lists the settled TV-only scope as an open question, misattributes the scope clarification, and has ownerless generic actions. D is concise but its action items are mostly invented and misattribute assignment distribution, with name and timestamp errors, making it the least reliable.
